sources.title: Human History Map: Northern Qi boundary metadata
sources.note: Local original GeoJSON inspected: northern-qi feature, 550 to 577, precision 1, coarse site-drawn outline after Tan Qixiang; bbox 110.5,32.2,126,42.5. This is evidence about the map, not independent historical authority.

sources.title: He Liqun and colleagues: Results of the 2021 excavations at Ye
sources.note: Direct Hebei Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology report read. Section 1 palace remains span Eastern Wei and Northern Qi; section 2 Dazhuangyan Temple founded Tianbao year 9 and building 9 plaster, paint and uncertain rooms. Drain 209 dimensions preserved exactly.

sources.title: Wang Wei: 2015 fieldwork of the CASS Institute of Archaeology
sources.note: Indexed original annual report read, Ye team subsection: Caocun kiln site 1.5 km east of inner east wall, three Northern Dynasties kilns, glazed pottery, celadon and kiln furniture; attribution to Eastern Wei and Northern Qi production. Direct fetch timed out.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Jar with floral decorations and musicians, 2002.268
sources.note: Direct museum record: late sixth century, Northern Qi attribution, stoneware with applied decoration under celadon glaze, 18.1 cm high. Curatorial text identifies Central Asian traditions. No excavation provenance claimed.

sources.title: Geng Shuo: Alterations to images in the Northern Qi tomb of Xu Xianxiu
sources.note: Full indexed original author/institutional republication of Palace Museum Journal 2022, no. 3. Direct fetch failed. Sections 1 and 3, figures 2, 3, 6 and 21: 571 tomb, banquet, repainted right eye, omitted flute, Lou Rui wet-plaster outlines. PDF download exceeded web tool limit.

sources.title: Yan Zhitui: Family Instructions for the Yan Clan, Chinese text
sources.note: Direct Chinese edition read, chapters 2, 3 and 5. Chapter 2 explicitly introduces a Northern Qi official and includes 我有一兒，年已十七. English rendering is a literal translation; also checked the same episode in Sanping Chen, Multicultural China in the Early Middle Ages, publisher-distributor preview. Modern digital edition, not an ancient manuscript witness.

sources.title: Xiaofei Tian: Family Instructions for the Yan Clan and Other Works by Yan Zhitui (2021)
sources.note: Indexed original scholarly publisher description read: Yan lived 531 to the 590s, served multiple courts, completed the work in his last years. Full translation not claimed read. All public Yan-derived text across this source, Gutenberg and Sterckx is pooled as one underlying work.

sources.title: Roel Sterckx: Excreted and left untreated? Human and animal waste: from Dunhuang to Laozi
sources.note: Direct Cambridge repository accepted manuscript, page 2, note 4. Explicitly calls Yan an early indirect reference to paper for hygiene; no invention date or universal custom. Yan chapter 5 Chinese independently checked.

sources.title: NYU Institute for the Study of the Ancient World: Selection of the Sutra of Immeasurable Meaning
sources.note: Direct exhibition object entry: Northern Group South Cave interior west wall, circa 572 to 577, FSC-R-565.2, two ink-on-paper rubbings; preserving scripture in stone and rubbing method. No unverified original-script reading taken from image.

sources.title: Smart Museum of Art: Echoes of the Past, Xiangtangshan
sources.note: Direct exhibition research description: cave sculptures removed in first half of twentieth century; project begun 2004; hundreds of overlapping scans and chisel/break matching. Pooled conservatively with NYU Echoes pages and the Northern Zhou packet’s 58 words from its map page.

sources.title: NYU Institute for the Study of the Ancient World: Northern Qi historical map
sources.note: Direct exhibition text: Emperor Wenxuan reigned 550 to 559. Used only for this reign interval; erroneous Gao Huan founder sentence omitted. Combined exhibit-work budget includes Northern Zhou existing 58 words.

proposedOverrides.name: Northern Qi
proposedOverrides.summary: The Gao dynasty ruled from Ye and sponsored influential Buddhist art before Northern Zhou conquered it in 577.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Exact seams index state, 550 to 577, capital Ye; no alias association. Eastern Wei is its predecessor; Northern Zhou is distinct.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: One site-drawn china-seams.geojson polygon, precision 1, bbox [110.5,32.2,126,42.5]. Public caution identifies coarse extent; no precise border inference.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Historical dynasty dates retained. Eastern Wei/Northern Qi palace and kiln evidence spans both phases explicitly. Yan’s final book is later than the map window and labelled accordingly. Late-sixth-century museum attribution has no invented point year.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact Chinese clause from chapter 2 of a modern edition of Yan; literal English translation, not an ancient manuscript photograph. Chapter begins by naming Northern Qi.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No claim of universal literacy, ordinary households resembling elite tombs, drains being universal sewers, or a dated invention of toilet paper. No unverified medical remedy added.
